Fed Minutes Hold Policy Clues. How to Decode Them. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Megan Leonhardt

Three weeks after each meeting of the Federal Reserve's policy-setting committee, the central bank releases a summary of the closed-door discussions that took place.

The minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee are inevitably stale, yet economists, market analysts, and other Fed watchers, Barron's included, pore over the details. It is a bit like watching a baseball game whose score you know, but you want to learn how that triple play in the fourth inning came together, and whether the latest trade could shake up the team's prospects. In this case, Fed followers want to know how much consensus exists on the committee for policy decisions, and what that might imply for future decisions, notably those regarding interest rates. That is particularly important under Kevin Warsh, who became the Fed's chairman in May, as Warsh has sworn off forward guidance, or telegraphing the Fed's future policy path. Actions may speak louder than words on the Warsh Fed, especially as the number of words issued by the FOMC has shrunk. Both the official policy statement issued after each FOMC meeting and the minutes have become shorter and more concise. Minutes of the June FOMC meeting ran at roughly 5,300 words; July's minutes were closer to 5,000, and those from the September meeting clocked in at about 4,800. In all cases, the meeting minutes were shorter than those released under former Fed Chair Jerome Powell, whom Warsh succeeded.

In the minutes of the Fed's Sept. 15-16 meeting, released on Oct. 7, officials were unified in deciding to raise rates by a quarter of a percentage point, to a target range of 3.75% to 4%. That marked a change from several prior meetings this year, which saw dissents to the committee's decision to hold rates steady.

The unanimous vote suggests a firmer commitment by the committee to bring down inflation, which has exceeded the Fed's 2% annual target for more than five years.

The minutes of the Jan. 27-28 FOMC meeting revealed that "several" participants supported changes to the postmeeting statement to reflect the possibility that an increase in interest rates might be warranted if inflation remained at above-target levels. By the July 28-29 meeting, that had shifted to "many" participants, who said policy tightening would likely be necessary if inflation didn't decline.

Generally, "several participants" carries more weight than "some" or a "few." These types of qualifiers can also signal a lack of consensus among the FOMC's 19 members, 12 of whom vote at meetings.

A divergence of viewpoints also surfaced in the September minutes, albeit around the rationale for potentially raising rates. The minutes highlighted that "many" officials emphasized that higher rates would be "prudent on risk-management grounds," acting as insurance against the possibility that inflation would remain high due to the risk of supply shocks. But "a number of participants" viewed higher rates as necessary based on their economic outlook, rather than as a risk-management measure.

At the next FOMC meeting, scheduled for Oct. 27-28, FOMC members will seek to determine how restrictive policy has become as higher rates take hold, and whether they need to raise interest rates further.

Warsh said at a press conference following the September meeting that he would be "hard-pressed to describe broad financial conditions as restrictive." He added that this view was widely shared by the committee.

The September minutes showed that "several" participants viewed policy as not restrictive or only mildly restrictive. They also indicated that officials finally pulled the trigger on raising rates because they believed that underlying inflation wouldn't decelerate and return to 2% without the Fed's intervention. Moreover, policymakers increasingly felt the economy was strong — or strong enough to tolerate higher interest rates.

The FOMC will meet again on Oct. 27-28. Futures markets put 81% odds on no change in rates, and 19% odds a quarter-point increase. The minutes, due Nov. 18, will recount how the committee voted, and more importantly, explain why.

Write to Megan Leonhardt at megan.leonhardt@barrons.com

Kalshi is investigating bets on Trump’s press secretary pick placed before announcement: WSJ
data.description:
Prediction market Kalshi is investigating a series of trades that correctly predicted President Donald Trump would pick conservative commentator Katie Zacharia as his next White House press secretary, The Wall Street Journal reported Friday.

A Kalshi spokesperson confirmed the probe to the Journal and declined to comment further. Trades on Kalshi are anonymous to the public, but the company keeps records of its traders' identities.

The New York Times and other outlets began reporting Zacharia's selection around 2 p.m. ET on Friday. At least three wagers on her were placed beforehand, according to a Journal analysis of publicly available Kalshi data.

A $19 bet placed around 10:42 p.m. ET on Thursday is slated to pay out $1,896 once the market closes. Two more bets, for about $74 and $80, were placed around 1:41 p.m. on Friday and are expected to pay out $3,689 and $4,023.

Kalshi traders gave Zacharia about a 1% chance of being named to the post in the days before the reports, according to the Journal. Trump confirmed the appointment in a Truth Social post on Friday afternoon, naming Zacharia to succeed Karoline Leavitt. "I am confident that Katie will deliver strong results for our Country," Trump wrote.

Zacharia is a senior communications adviser at Trump Media & Technology Group, which operates Truth Social. She previously served as a spokesperson and deputy assistant secretary for public affairs at the Department of Homeland Security, according to Trump's post.

Insider trading on prediction markets

The White House did not return the Journal's request for comment, and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) did not respond before the Journal's publication. The White House previously sent staff a memo warning them against using nonpublic information for private gain after a series of well-timed bets related to the Iran war, the Journal reported.

In August, former White House teleprompter operator Gabriel Perez agreed to repay $107,539 in profits and pay a $65,000 civil penalty to settle CFTC charges that he traded Kalshi mention markets after reading Trump's prepared remarks. The CFTC credited Kalshi with assisting in the case.

Kalshi also permanently banned former Rep. George Santos on Aug. 31 over trades tied to his State of the Union attendance and fined him just over $71,000. Santos had agreed in July to pay $35,000 to settle with the CFTC over the same bet, without admitting or denying the agency's findings.

In June, Kalshi began requiring traders to disclose their employers before trading in markets it deems at heightened risk of insider trading or manipulation. The company said at the time it had made more than 20 law enforcement referrals and opened more than 150 investigations in the first quarter.

House Oversight Committee Chair James Comer opened a probe into insider trading on Kalshi and Polymarket in May, requesting documents on how the platforms verify identities and detect unusual trading.

The Block has reached out to Kalshi and the White House for comment.

data.title: The $60 Million Wedding You Never Heard Of — and the Stealth Rich Class Behind It — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Andy Serwer

Here's a tale of two over-the-top weddings — one familiar, the other probably not.

The first was Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sanchez's black-tie, star-studded (the usual Kardashians, DiCaprio, and Gates crowd) extravaganza in Venice last year. The festivities, which essentially took over the city and sparked protests, included a Gatsby-themed party. Cost: an estimated $50 million.

The second wedding was a five-day celebration in Paris two years earlier, which included a rehearsal dinner at the Paris Opera House, fireworks at the Eiffel Tower, and a party under the Arc de Triomphe. There was also a night at the Palace of Versailles, leased entirely for the soiree, where guests dined in the style of the lost monarchy, served by waiters dressed in period costume. Adam Levine of Maroon Five performed "She Will Be Loved" for the couple's first dance. Cost: upward of $60 million.

Eye roll alert. Must be another Silicon Valley or Wall Street arriviste, right? Wrong. As it turns out, the second wedding was thrown by Robert and Paula Brockway of Coral Gables, Fla., for their daughter Madelaine. The Brockways are car dealers.

The anecdote of the Brockway's "Wedding of the Century" (though not the groom's legal travails) comes from The Everywhere Millionaire: Who Is Really Rich in America and How They Got There, a new book by Owen Zidar and Eric Zwick, Princeton University and University of Chicago economists, respectively. The Brockway nuptials illustrate the fact that the great majority of rich people in America aren't rubbing shoulders with Sand Hill Road venture capitalists or subordinating debentures. They got rich running their own businesses, be it a string of Ford dealerships, a medical office, or, as The Wall Street Journal reported recently, a restaurant-supply business.

"Celebrity billionaires monopolize all the attention," Zidar tells me from his office in Princeton, N.J. "Yes, there are very rich people, like Sam Altman and Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos. But if you add up all of their wealth, it's an order of magnitude smaller than millionaires who own private businesses."

As of 2022, the authors say, there were three million such millionaires — people with $5 million or more who own a private business — worth $54.8 trillion. That same year, the entire Forbes 400 was worth only $4 trillion. (Both numbers have doubtless spiked since then.) Small wonder that the American consumer, particularly on the high end, is still going great guns.

Zidar calls them Everywhere Millionaires because they aren't clustered in Manhattan or Menlo Park, Calif. "There are rich people all across America," he says. "I used to go to a lake in the Ozarks, and people had $100,000 boats left and right. Those are the people we're talking about."

Intuitively, none of this is particularly earth-shattering, but before the professors' work, no one had quantified this phenomenon. That, says Zidar, is another reason why we focus on the big company CEOs. "Those companies report CEO pay; private business owners don't," he says.

Key to the rise of the Everywhere Millionaire class (and to the book) has been the proliferation over the past 40 years of "pass through" businesses (mentioned 165 times in the text). Pass-throughs don't pay corporate taxes. Instead, any profits pass through to their owners' individual income taxes. In recent decades, lower tax rates for pass-throughs have driven business owners to adopt them.

The Treasury Department hired Zidar and Zwick in 2014, fresh out of graduate school (they lived in an apartment owned by an artist who decorated with exhibits of Peeps, the Easter candy), to help figure out how much business owners were paying in taxes. "That data proved a gold mine," they write. "With it, we discovered a hidden world of rich business owners....We could fill out the full map of American enterprise...and see who owned what, how much they earned, where they lived, and how they built their fortunes."

A recent look at the Bloomberg Billionaire list shows a cluster of seven Anthropic execs (including the Amodei siblings, Dario and Daniela), each worth $7.98 billion. Right below, at $7.91 billion, is Johnny Morris, founder of Bass Pro Shops. Hard to believe in this day and age, but it's Morris who's more typical, not the Amodeis.

Write to Andy Serwer at andy.serwer@barrons.com. Follow him on X and subscribe to his At Barron's podcast.

data.title: AI Loves Walmart — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Teresa Rivas

Who says the big boxes are dead?

A study by UBS analyst Michael Lasser revealed that artificial-intelligence shopping agents recommended the biggest retailers more often than not. Digitally native merchants? Out of luck.

The UBS team submitted a dozen identical shopping prompts to ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Muse in three areas: New Jersey, New York, and Minnesota. The findings: "AI recommendations generally reinforce established industry leadership," he writes, with Walmart leading the list, followed by Costco Wholesale.

Per Lasser, Walmart was frequently the top recommendation and the secondary one as well, across categories from groceries to auto parts: "This suggests that AI models increasingly view Walmart as a default answer for everyday consumption."

Costco, meanwhile, wasn't suggested "because of convenience or immediacy. Instead, it was...associated with value, quality, and bulk purchasing," Lasser writes. Costco's "brand equity has become deeply embedded within the information ecosystem."

Being the best at something did pay. For instance: Dick's Sporting Goods and Aldi popped up frequently, which Lasser attributes to their leadership in their corners of the industry and reputation for value.

Still, it wasn't all bad news for those left out. Recommendations were more varied in categories where availability was location-dependent, or no retailer was the obvious winner. This includes big categories like furniture and Korean beauty products.

The upshot: In the AI world, there's still market share up for grabs.

Write to Teresa Rivas at teresa.rivas@barrons.com

Last Week

Happy Stocks

The "What, Me Worry?" market finished the week higher despite angst over the bond market and the Strait of Hormuz. The S&P 500 hit a new high on Tuesday, slumped, then rebounded on Friday to close the week up 1.15%, thanks, again, to AI and bullish earnings forecasts.

La Détresse

Budget talks begin soon in France, which is under siege by student protesters demanding more education funding and, you know, bond traders. The French budget deficit is a worrisome 5.1% or so of GDP. Could it default on its national debt? Who knows? Cuts to the country's generous social programs seem inevitable.

Fed Friendly

The minutes from the September Federal Open Market Committee meeting were a snooze. But it was worth noting, per Barron's Megan Leonhardt, that the decision to raise rates wasn't only unanimous, but unusually without rancor. And most members were keen on another increase by year end. Data panic alert: September CPI will be out Wednesday.

High Courts

The Supreme Court Monday tackled Suncor Energy v. Board of County Commissioners of Boulder County. Can plaintiffs sue in state court for climate-change damages? Suncor says it's a federal matter. Colorado's high court ruled for the plaintiffs. Justice Samuel Alito recused, so a 4-4 outcome is in play, which would be a victory for Boulder.

Next Week

Monday 10/12

Fixed-income markets are closed in?observance of Columbus Day.

Tuesday 10/13

Third-quarter earnings season commences, with financials leading the?way. Citigroup, JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs Group, and Wells Fargo release quarterly results on Tuesday, followed by Bank of America, BlackRock, and Morgan Stanley on Wednesday, and Charles Schwab and Interactive Brokers Group on Thursday. Outside of financials, Johnson & Johnson and UnitedHealth Group announce earnings on Tuesday.

Wednesday 10/14

The Bureau of Labor Statistics releases the consumer price index for September. Consensus estimate is for a?3.6% year-over-year increase, two-tenths of a percentage point more than in August. The core CPI is expected to rise 2.5% from 2.4% previously.

Thursday 10/15

The Census Bureau reports retail sales data for September. Economists forecast a 0.3% month-over-month gain, after a 1.1% jump in August. Excluding autos and gas, sales are seen?rising 0.2%.

The Numbers

3.2%

Projected rise in real global GDP in 2026 as the AI boom cushions the effects of inflation. For 2027, 3.1%.

$49.2 B

Wall Street's bonus pool in 2025, a record. This year's haul should top that as industry profits head to $90 billion.

10,814

Registrations of China's Jaecoo 7 in the United Kingdom in September as the SUV topped U.K. vehicle sales.

780%

Increase in Samsung Electronics' quarterly operating profit, reflecting ferocious demand for memory chips.

Write to editors@barrons.com

data.title: Larsen & Toubro shares: 114% return in 5 yrs, Motilal Oswal sees 19% more upside stock | Target price
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- Larsen & Toubro share price target: Shares of Larsen & Toubro Limited, have delivered 114% return over the last five years, but the capital goods stock has rarely surged over the last one year. Larsen & Toubro is likely to benefit from strong execution, ramp up in domestic orders, and focused execution, according to Motilal Oswal Financial Services, which sees nearly 19% upside potential in the stock.

L&T stock closed nearly 1.2% higher on Friday, however, its share price value has declined 10.6% in 2026 so far.

The company is focusing on higher fabrication in India for its projects and is ramping up execution in domestic and large private projects to offset weakness due to the ongoing West Asia crisis, as per Motilal Oswal.

"Despite the ongoing crisis in the Middle East, inflows from that region have ramped up sharply for LT, and out of the total announced order inflows of ~INR1.3t so far in 2QFY27, projects worth ~INR775b were announced from the Middle East," stated the brokerage in its report.

L&T's order inflows have surged sharply over the past few months. The company has diversified beyond the Middle East too for orders from international geographies such as Europe, Africa, Canada and now targeting North Asia, South Korea, Japan and Taiwan.

"With a prospect pipeline of INR15t for 9MFY27 and an order book of INR7.8t as of Jun'26, we expect LT's core EPC order inflows/revenue to grow at 10%/14% CAGR over FY26-29," read the MOFSL report.

The brokerage gave a 'Buy' rating for the stock with a target price of Rs.4,400 per share. "We maintain our SoTP-based TP of INR4,400, based on 25x on Dec'28E earnings for the core business and a 25% holding company discount to subsidiaries."

The stock closed 2.17% higher at Rs.3699.10 per share on BSE on Friday, October 9. Its share price value has declined 5% in six months, 1.86% in one year. But the stock has delivered 6% return in two years, 20% return in three years and 114% return in five years.

data.title: HCL Tech Q2 results 2026 preview, expectations: Will IT giant deliver strong growth? Profit, revenue, dividend history
data.description:
HCL Tech Q2 results, Oct. 10 -- Days after IT bellwether Tata Consultancy Services Limited announced promising performance in the second quarter of financial year 2026-27, investors will closely track HCL Technologies Q2 result announcement, scheduled for Monday, October 12. The IT heavyweight may see single digit revenue growth driven by IT and engineering research and development, as per experts.

The Noida-headquartered IT services giant firm will announce its Q2FY27 result post-closing of Indian stock markets on Monday. Here's what experts expect for HCL Tech Q2 result 2026.

HCL Technologies revenue is likely to grow 2.4% (in constant currency terms) sequentially in the quarter ending in September, 2026, according to brokerage PL Capital. Motilal Oswal sees a 3% QoQ growth in services revenue (CC), which is likely to reflect contribution of around 1% from Jaspersoft and the HPE Telco business.

"We expect HCLT revenue to increase by 2.4% QoQ in CC & 2.3% in USD terms, with 1.2% QoQ CC organic growth & contribution from Jaspersoft and HPE acquisitions," stated PL Capital in its report.

The IT firm's EBIT margin may expand nearly 70 bp on a quarterly basis, supported by revenue growth and FX tailwind, as per Nuvama report. However, MOFSL is expecting 120 bp expansion in EBIT margin.

"EBIT margin is expected to expand ~120bp QoQ to ~18.1%, in line with the usual 2Q seasonal improvement, as we do not expect incremental investment headwinds," read the Motilal Oswal Financial Services report.

As per Nuvama report, the IT services giant may see 15.9% year-on-year growth in its profit after tax (PAT), and 6.2% on a QoQ basis. Motilal Oswal sees 21.3% YoY jump in PAT.

While Nuvama expects FY27 guidance revision by HCL Technologies, PL Capital sees the IT firm to "maintain mid-range of its FY27E organic guidance."

"We expect HCLT to tweak its FY27 Services guidance to 2.5%-4.0% (from 1.5-4.5%) CC YoY maintaining the mid-point. EBIT margin guidance is likely to be trimmed to lower half of 17.5-18.5% range," read Motilal Oswal report.

The Shiv Nadar-led IT giant paid Rs.54 per equity share dividend in FY26, and an annual payout of Rs.60 per share in FY25. HCL Tech payout stood at Rs.52 per share in FY 24. With this, its dividend yield stood at 4.1% in FY26, 4.6% in FY25, and 4.0% in FY24, as per SBI Securities report.

The stock closed 2.84% higher at Rs.1214.30 per share on BSE with an Mcap of Rs.3,29,520.35 crore. Its stock value has declined 11.8% in one year and 11% in two years.

data.title: Meet Rakesh Kumar: Indian Oil executive recommended for CPCL's Director of Operations post
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- Rakesh Kumar, a senior Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) executive, has received a board-level recommendation. The Public Enterprises Selection Board recommended him as Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited's Director of Operations.

Rakesh Kumar currently serves as General Manager of Technical Services at Indian Oil Corporation Limited. His professional background covers oil refining, technical operations and management of downstream petroleum activities.

The recommendation could bring a major step forward in his career. However, his appointment still needs final approval from the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet.

The selection board's recommendation will now go before the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet. This committee must give final approval before Kumar takes charge.

Once approved, he will become CPCL's Director of Operations. For now, his selection remains a recommendation awaiting that decision.

Rakesh Kumar is a petroleum sector professional with experience in the industry. His work has focused on refinery operations, engineering and improving technical processes.

These areas form a part of his profile. His experience includes work with India's government-owned energy companies.

At IOCL, he holds a position in technical services. The proposed CPCL role would take him into the company's board-level leadership.

The selection followed a competitive panel interview conducted by the Public Enterprises Selection Board. Kumar was chosen from among nine candidates representing major public-sector oil and gas companies, according to PSU Connect.

The panel also interviewed senior executives from IOCL, CPCL and Oil and Natural Gas Corporation. Their roles covered operations, production, human resources, planning and other business functions.

Among the IOCL candidates was Kondapalli Siva Rama Rao, Chief General Manager and CEO of IOLPL. M Sankar, Chief General Manager in the Chairman's Secretariat, also appeared before the panel.

Muralidhar S represented IOCL as Chief General Manager for LPG at its Karnataka State Office. Om Prasad Chetry, General Manager in charge of human resources, was another IOCL candidate.

CPCL candidates included Purushotham, Chief General Manager for Corporate Planning and Business Development. Thullibilli Kishor Babu, General Manager of Operations, was also interviewed.

ONGC candidates included Bhishmadev Mandal, Chief General Manager of Production. Om Prakash, General Manager overseeing Operations and Maintenance Contracts, also appeared for the interview.

Director of Operations is a Schedule 'A' board-level position at CPCL. The director oversees the refinery's operations and related company functions.

CPCL is an IOCL subsidiary and a petroleum refining company in South India. The position comes under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.

data.title: Tennessee execution survivor Christa Pike released from hospital, returned to prison
data.description:
Death row inmate Christa Pike was released from a US hospital on Saturday and sent back to prison where she will continue receiving medical care following her botched execution attempt in Tennessee, her attorneys said.

Pike was discharged from a local hospital and is now at the Debra K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center, where she has been housed for more than 30 years, said attorneys Stephen Ferrell and Luke Ihnen from Federal Defender Services of Eastern Tennessee, and Randy Spivey and Kelly Gleason from the Tennessee Office of the Post Conviction Defender in a joint release.

Pike, sentenced to death for a 1995 murder, awoke "angry and confused" in the hospital this week with a long recuperation ahead after surviving the attempted execution on September 30, her lawyers said on Wednesday. They previously believed she could be brain-dead.

Pike, 50, had been taken from the execution chamber to a Nashville hospital, unconscious, critically ill and ‌with severe arm injuries after two injections failed to kill her at the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution.

A Tennessee judge this week ordered state officials to preserve all evidence related to their failed attempt to execute her, a development one of her lawyers called the "first of many steps to preserve and enforce her constitutional rights."

Tennessee Governor Bill Lee suspended all executions for the rest of the year while investigators look in to the botched execution of Pike and a similar failure involving Tony Carruthers in May, when prison officials were unable to set up intravenous ​lines.

data.title: Justin Sun Shares AI and Quantum Vision at TOKEN2049 Singapore and Blockworks DAS Asia
data.description:
Geneva, Switzerland, October 10, 2026 — TRON DAO, the community-governed DAO dedicated to accelerating the decentralization of the internet through blockchain technology and decentralized applications (dApps), participated in TOKEN2049 Singapore as Title Sponsor and in Blockworks’ Digital Asset Summit (DAS) Asia 2026 at the Marina Bay Sands. TRON Founder Justin Sun joined fireside discussions at both conferences, sharing his views on stablecoins, institutional adoption, AI-driven commerce, machine-to-machine payments and the need for quantum-resilient blockchain infrastructure.

On October 7, Sun joined Michael Ippolito, Co-Founder of Blockworks, on the main stage at DAS Asia 2026 for a fireside titled “In Conversation with Justin Sun.” Organized by Blockworks, DAS Asia is an institution-focused digital asset conference examining the intersection of traditional finance and the digital asset economy. The conversation covered the evolution of stablecoins, institutional adoption, agentic AI payments and TRON’s role in the global digital asset economy.

Sun highlighted the growing role of tokenized assets and stablecoins as practical financial infrastructure, particularly for cross-border payments and access to digital dollars and U.S.-based assets. He also discussed the emerging role of AI agents in the economy, predicting that within the near future, AI agents will increasingly make payments, purchase digital services and manage financial activity on behalf of users.

On October 8, Sun joined Kevin Follonier, Founder of When Shift Happens, for “Fireside Chat with Justin Sun” on the TOKEN2049 main stage. The discussion explored the future of blockchain, stablecoins, AI agents and the broader evolution of global finance. Sun also discussed the need to prepare blockchain networks for quantum computing, noting that TRON has already made meaningful progress toward post-quantum readiness, with end-to-end post-quantum signature support deployed on the Nile testnet.

Furthermore, pointing to the mathematics behind the cryptography that secures blockchain networks, Sun turned to the Justin Sun Prize, which he describes as the “Nobel Prize of the AI Era.” Structured as a zero-trust, decentralized academic bounty mechanism built around a “problem list,” the prize recognizes breakthroughs in fundamental disciplines verified through machine formal verification. It seeks to accelerate fundamental research through collaboration between humans and AI.

“AI agents using crypto will become the industry’s biggest use case within the next five years,” said Sun. “As AI agents begin to transact, pay and operate autonomously, blockchain will become the financial infrastructure behind them. TRON’s focus is to provide the fast, efficient and accessible settlement layer that can support this next generation of global finance.”

TRON DAO also hosted a dedicated booth at the conference, giving attendees the opportunity to connect with the broader TRON community and learn about the ecosystem’s work across stablecoin payments, decentralized applications and AI-driven financial infrastructure. Beyond the conference floor, TRON DAO also hosted a Creators and Media Networking Happy Hour, welcoming industry leaders for an evening of light bites and conversation.

Across both events, the discussions underscored TRON’s focus on building blockchain infrastructure for a rapidly evolving financial system being shaped by stablecoins, tokenized assets, AI agents and increasingly resilient digital-asset networks.

About TRON DAO

TRON DAO is a community-governed DAO dedicated to accelerating the decentralization of the internet via blockchain technology and dApps.

Founded in September 2017, the TRON blockchain has experienced significant growth since its MainNet launch in May 2018. Today, TRON hosts the largest circulating supply of USD Tether (USDT) stablecoin, which currently exceeds $94 billion. As of October 2026, the TRON blockchain has recorded over 407 million in total user accounts, more than 15 billion in total transactions, and over $28 billion in total value locked (TVL), based on TRONSCAN. Recognized as the global settlement layer for stablecoin transactions and everyday purchases with proven success, TRON is “Moving Trillions, Empowering Billions.”

data.title: How a Western Consumer Giant Is Thriving on China's Social-Media Shoppers — WSJ
data.description:
By Natasha Khan

Several years ago, China-based executives of Lysol maker Reckitt leveled with their boss. More consumers were skipping supermarket runs and buying household staples while they scrolled on their phones, the executives said.

Could they have some funds to get ahead of the trend?

Chief Executive Kris Licht figured they were talking about China's equivalents of Amazon.com and Walmart+. "But no," Licht recalled in an interview, "I was told that e-commerce was a yesterday technology."

The result: a pivot in Reckitt's China sales tactics, one that has propelled 12 consecutive quarters of double-digit sales growth in the country and helped the British firm weather a sales slowdown in established markets.

What the CEO's colleagues said Reckitt needed to jump on was the rapid rise of a different venue for shopping in China. In what's known as social commerce, people scrolling through their social media apps for entertainment end up buying after seeing an ad.

Reckitt's success capitalizing on Chinese consumers' shift points to how Western firms that once counted on China for growth can still thrive there, though local competitors have made it a tougher place to do business. It's also an example of how social media and shopping are converging.

After its China team's tête-à-tête with Licht, Reckitt pulled out the stops to go to the social media apps where many Chinese wind up shopping.

The company built 18 studios inside a five-story building on the outskirts of Shanghai. On videos broadcast from there, employees sell Veet hair removal cream, Lysol's international equivalent Dettol and other Reckitt goods on China's popular social-media platforms.

In some of the studios, company staffers join guest actors and influencers making quick comedies and mini-dramas about domestic life featuring a Reckitt brand.

"This is the way forward," Licht said. "Those that don't figure this out will be left behind."

Some 800 million of China's 1.4 billion people now each day use social media like Douyin, the Chinese version of TikTok, and apps like Kuaishou. The users spend an average of about 90 minutes a day scrolling through short videos, Reckitt estimated. Key for consumer-good companies: Half of them have bought items on the platforms.

Social commerce is starting to catch on in the U.S., where shoppers are now buying products by clicking links in TikTok and Instagram videos, and watching live-shopping streams on apps like Whatnot.

"We all have the experience of finishing the day, relaxing on the sofa, watching videos and clicking 'buy' without thinking too much about it," said Vivien Huang, Reckitt's director of marketing in China. "Next thing you know, you wake up with some new products at your doorstep."

It was around 2022 that Reckitt's team in China sought Licht's support getting Reckitt to invest in social commerce.

The team initially struggled to hire influencers or agencies with the right experience, so staff did it themselves. Out of a conference room converted into a makeshift studio, customer-service staff answered questions on video about the chemical composition of disinfectants.

Sales shot up, boosting the company while it grappled with stagnating sales in the U.S. and other developed markets. Reckitt's emerging-market sales grew 8.5% to 2.23 billion pounds, equivalent to $2.95 billion, in the first half of this year, compared with the same period a year prior, while inching up 0.8% in North America and falling 3% in Europe.

The company's success in China makes it an outlier among big Western brands. After years of rapid expansion, consumer companies from Starbucks to LVMH to Nike have stumbled as consumer preferences have shifted and competition from local brands has increased. Also cutting into sales of Western firms are the economy's slower growth.

Reckitt's China livestream strategy "enabled its brands to hold their own against steep local competition," said Sky Canaves, an analyst at Emarketer. "It's part of a broader commitment to deeply localizing its brands, and positions digital as the primary sales channel, rather than relying on traditional store distribution as the foundation."

From the company's Shanghai studios, crews broadcast live on the apps for 12 hours a day, while shoppers bombard them with comments and questions in a chat that dominates part of the screen.

The Reckitt hosts respond rapidly, a sort of interactive infomercial. A team monitoring the livestreams guides the hosts and adjusts the featured products they talk about in real-time.

In other studios, short dramas and skits are filmed. The videos, which are often under a minute, might depict a scene from a living room or highlight a domestic dispute. In one, a parent argues with their teenager about smelly shoes — and Dettol comes to the rescue.

The short-form video team drove 40 million new customers to Reckitt last year, drawn by videos they produced that the company said were viewed 15 billion times.

Reckitt predicts social commerce will catch on in some form in the more than 100 other countries where it sells its products, and has begun replicating its China playbook in markets including Brazil, Mexico and Malaysia.

Write to Natasha Khan at natasha.khan@wsj.com

data.title: Smartphone Makers See India Demand Holding Up Despite Rising Costs
data.description:
Xiaomi, Motorola and iQOO point to evolving consumer preferences for advanced processors, AI features and improved smartphone experiences despite higher component costs

India continues to be a key growth market for global smartphone manufacturers, with demand holding up despite rising memory and storage costs pushing up handset prices. Companies are seeing consumers place greater emphasis on advanced processors, artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities and overall user experience as smartphone purchasing preferences evolve.

At the 10th edition of India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 in New Delhi, executives from Xiaomi, Motorola and iQOO highlighted these changing consumer preferences and outlined their upcoming flagship devices during interactions on the sidelines of a Qualcomm event at Yashobhoomi.

Gautam Batra, Associate Director – Product Marketing at Xiaomi, said consumers had adjusted to sustained increases in component costs and the resulting revisions in smartphone prices. Despite higher prices for random-access memory (RAM) and storage, the company continued to see healthy demand, suggesting that buyers had adapted to the changing pricing environment.

Batra described India as an important market for Xiaomi and other original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), citing its growth potential and consumers' aspirations for more advanced smartphones. He said the Indian market was growing faster than several other markets, reinforcing its importance to the company's business strategy.

On the product front, Batra said Xiaomi's newly unveiled Xiaomi 18 Pro flagship would feature Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 platform across international and Indian markets. The device is expected to offer improvements in graphics processing, photography and AI performance.

Motorola also highlighted changing consumer expectations, with buyers increasingly assessing smartphones on the quality of the experience they offer rather than technical specifications alone. Shivam Ranjan, Marketing Head – APAC at Motorola, said Indian consumers were becoming more discerning and placing greater emphasis on human-centric features and practical usability.

Ranjan previewed Motorola's upcoming Signature 27 handset, scheduled for release in 2026. The device is expected to be among the early smartphones powered by Qualcomm's Snapdragon 6 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset. Its planned features include camera capabilities, agentic AI and a design intended to address evolving consumer requirements.

Meanwhile, iQOO announced its upcoming flagship, the iQOO 16, which will be powered by Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 platform. Nipun Marya, CEO of iQOO, said the smartphone would launch in India soon and represent the company's fastest device to date.

Marya added that further details of the company's collaboration with Qualcomm would be announced at a later stage.

data.title: Two Dead After Isaias Crashes Into Gulf Coast — WSJ
data.description:
By Joseph Pisani

Two people are dead and hundreds of thousands of customers were without power Saturday afternoon after Isaias crashed into the U.S. Gulf Coast overnight, bringing heavy rain and strong winds even as it moved inland.

The deaths happened in separate incidents in Alabama and Florida after trees fell on their homes, authorities said.

Isaias made landfall Friday night near Destin, Fla., as a Category 2 hurricane with 105 mph winds that downed trees and knocked out power lines. It has weakened as it grinds north through Alabama, with winds at about 35 mph. The storm was categorized as a posttropical cyclone Saturday and is expected to subside Sunday, the National Weather Service said.

Nearly 800,000 customers remained without electricity Saturday afternoon in Alabama, Florida and Georgia, according to outage tracker PowerOutage.com. Florida accounted for more than half of the outages. Gov. Ron DeSantis said Saturday that crews were sent out overnight to begin repair work.

"We'll get everything back up and running and let people go on with their lives as soon as possible," DeSantis said Saturday morning.

Even as Isaias weakens, the storm is expected to drop as much as 8 inches of rain over the weekend in southern Alabama, the Florida Panhandle and southwest Georgia, forecasters said.

Rivers in the western Florida Panhandle could flood as they reach their highest levels Saturday and begin to recede Sunday, the National Weather Service said.

Isaias was the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 in what has been a relatively quiet season in the region. Forecasters are tracking two other storms elsewhere: Hurricane Simon off Mexico's west coast, and Tropical Storm Rachel that is headed toward the U.S.-Mexico border.

Two airports in the region, Destin-Fort Walton Beach Airport and the Pensacola International Airport, remained closed to clear and assess damage. Roads in parts of southern Alabama were closed and officials told people to stay home as crews worked to remove downed trees.

Write to Joseph Pisani at joseph.pisani@wsj.com

data.title: China passenger vehicle retail market slumps 24% in September
data.description:
An YTD slump in the passenger vehicle market in China extended last month, with retail sales for September totaling roughly 1.7M, a 24% decline from a year ago, according to preliminary data released by the China Passenger Car Association on Saturday.

While YTD retail sales fell 21% YoY to ~13.4M, the broader passenger vehicle market expanded from August, with passenger vehicle retail sales climbing ~10% from a month ago, driven by new energy vehicles.

Retail sales of passenger NEVs stood at ~1.1M in September, down ~12% YoY but accounting for ~67% of total passenger vehicle retail sales for the month.

YTD retail NEV sales totaled ~7.8M, down 12% YoY and signaling a weak domestic market, while wholesale passenger NEV sales reached ~11.4M YTD, up 10% from a year ago, as CPCA said higher oil prices remained elevated longer than expected, fueling exports.

The local markets also faced tough comps from a year earlier when sales climbed thanks to a rush to buy new vehicles before some Chinese regions reined in trade-in subsidies.

BYD , Geely Auto , Chery , Leapmotor , and Tesla were among the top 10 manufacturers in the passenger NEV wholesale market last month.

Companies including XPeng , Li Auto , and Nio were ranked outside the top ten.

data.title: Archery Premier League: Prithviraaj Yodhas clinch stunning 'Sudden Death' win against Chero Archers
data.description:
Hyderabad, Oct. 10 -- The full extent of the Archery Premier League's thrill was witnessed on Day three of the second season as Prithviraaj Yodhas handed Chero Archers their first defeat in a match that required multiple 'Sudden Death' situations to decide the winner here on Saturday.

In the day's first match, Mighty Marathas finally registered their first win of the season by beating Chola Chiefs 6-0. In the third match, defending champions Rajputana Royals suffered back-to-back defeats as they went down against Kakatiya Knights, who received plenty of backing from the local crowd at People's Plaza on Necklace Road, as per a press release.

In what was the match of the day, and the season so far, Yodhas first had to make it 4-4 in regulation time by winning Set 4 against the in-form Archers. In the first tiebreaker - APL's unique hit-or-miss shootoff - saw all four archers from both teams shoot outside the inner yellow ring, which registered as 'misses'. Then, the match went into Sudden Death with one archer from each side alternating to decide the winner on an immediate hit-or-miss basis, and it was Mexican recurve star Matias Grande who nailed the inner-ring hit to win it for Yodhas in the third Sudden Death while Prithika Pradeep couldn't do the same for her side.

For Chero, Kumkum Mohod - featuring for the first time after her Asian Games golden run - hit some impressive arrows but it was not enough for their side.

"This is a very small target. A little bit of luck, it was a good shot. In the first season it was smaller, and this time, it is more achievable I think. We are happy with the win. Honestly, it is a very special feeling, but it is not who gets the arrow to win the match, it is a team win," Grande said after the match.

The world's first franchise-based archery league, APL, is initiated by the Archery Association of India and comprises six teams and a total of 48 archers, with 36 Indians and 12 elite international stars. The league, taking place at People's Plaza in Hyderabad, will culminate on October 18 with the grand finale featuring the top four teams in the semifinals, followed by the title clash.

Earlier in the day, after losing both their opening matches, Mighty Marathas came alive in some style to beat Chola Chiefs comprehensively without dropping a single set. The Marathas, led by Mike Schloesser and anchored by Dhiraj Bommadevara under time pressure, beat Chiefs 6-0 for their first win of the tournament, while Chiefs have now suffered two defeats in three matches.

Schloesser, nicknamed 'Mr. Perfect', lived up to the billing as he shot 10s with all six arrows for Marathas.

The Chiefs stuck to their tactic from Day 2 as they opted for their compound archers to shoot back-to-back at the start of the set. But Chikitha Taniparthi's two 9s meant they couldn't impose the same sort of scoreboard pressure on their opponents. Marathas' recurve archers shot a couple of 8s but their compound archers had done enough to ensure they take the first set 74-73.

In the second set, Marathas' star recurve archer Dhiraj Bommadevara came up with a super 10 under pressure of the clock winding down and the Mighty Marathas took a 4-0 lead. It was another set of 9s for Taniparthi in the second set, which prompted the Chiefs to unsurprisingly bring on Colombia's Alejandra Usquiano, who was on fire on the second day.

In the third set, after a decent start from the compound archers, Deepika Kumari and Marcus D'Almeida couldn't keep the pressure on as they erred outside of the yellow zone on the target. The Marathas held it steady to take a low-scoring set 74-72 and ensure the match was wrapped up even before the fourth set.

In the final match, Asian Games recurve bronze medallist Neeraj Chauhan was the star for Kakatiya Knights as he came up with clutch X-ring 10s while local hero Jyothi Surekha Vennam was also on fire. While Tokyo Olympic champion Mete Gazoz helped Royals take the first set with a pressure 10 in the first set, it was Neeraj and Vennam who led the Knights to a fine come-from-behind 6-2 win. Knights, in fact, had the chance to shoot the Perfect 80 in the fourth set but the last arrow ended up being a 9, even though it was more than sufficient.

Up next on Sunday, the Chero Archers will look to continue their strong start to the season as they take on local franchise Kakatiya Knights. Chola Chiefs will have to bounce back when they face Prithviraaj Yodhas. In the final match, the rejuvenated Mighty Marathas go up against defending champions Rajputana Royals.

The Archery Premier League Season 2 is being broadcast on Sony LIV, Doordarshan, Archery Association of India YouTube, and Archery+. Tickets are available on District by Zomato.

SCORES: DAY 3 (October 10)

Match 1: Mighty Marathas 6-0 Chola Chiefs

Match 2: Prithviraaj Yodhas 4-4 (1-0 Sudden Death) Chero Archers

Match 3: Kakatiya Knights 6-2 Rajputana Royals

Recurve male: Neeraj Chauhan

Recurve female: Ankita Bhakat

Compound male: Rajat Chauhan

data.title: Diamond Power, Finolex, Polycab: How cables and wire stocks will perform in Q2 results 2026 | Expectations, preview
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- Diamond Power, Finolex, RR Kabel, Polycab shares: Wires and Cables sector companies are likely to post a strong quarter on value-led growth. Diamond Power Infrastructure Limited and Finolex Cables are likely to outperform peers, according to InCred Equities report. Other than these two, Polycab India, KEI, RR Kabel may also see double digit growth in the second quarter of financial year 2026-27.

Additionally, the brokerage hasn't seen any material impact on the industry players since the launch of Ultravolt, UltraTech Cement's cable business.

As higher copper and aluminium prices get passed through and volumes stay in low to mid-single digit, the segment is likely to witness another robust quarter, as per InCred Equities report. The segment is expected to see value-led growth.

Polycab India is expected to see growth across its cables and wires, FMEG & EPC segments with revenue likely to surge nearly 39% on an annual basis. The company's EBITDA may jump 20% on an annual basis, however, margin may fall 215 basis points annually to 13.6% due to the high inventory gain base during the quarter. The stock closed 1.21% higher at Rs.8250 per share on Friday, October 9.

"Strong volume and value-led growth is expected to sustain for the cable and wire segment for Polycab India, with FMEG and EPC segments expected to report double-digit growth as well. We reckon EBITDA margin at ~13.6%, with a PAT growth of 22%, for the quarter," stated the brokerage in its report.

The company's revenue growth may jump 27% on an annual basis, whereas EBITDA is likely to grow by 48% on an annual basis on better product mix. "Margin in 2QFY27F is expected to be ~11.5% (vs ~9.9% yoy) due to a favourable product mix. PAT is expected to grow by ~40% yoy for the quarter." KEI Industries share price closed 1.01% lower at Rs.4583.00 per share on Friday.

RR Kabel may post 39% annual jump in its revenue growth and EBITDA may improve by 48% on an annual basis. However its profit after tax (PAT) may decline around 16% on a quarterly basis, as per InCred report. "RR Kabel is expected to continue its growth momentum in 2QFY27F supported by C&W segment, with FMEG growing by ~21% yoy," stated the brokerage. The stock closed 0.46% higher at Rs.2705.30 per share.

Finolex Cables is likely to post 38% annual growth led by electrical cable segment and the high growth communications segment. "EBITDA margin is expected to be ~10.9%, driven by a better product mix and operating leverage. PAT is expected to grow by ~10% yoy for the quarter." Finolex Cables stock closed 0.83% lower at Rs.1390.25 per share.

The brokerage expects, the company to maintain its strong momentum in Q2, especially in MT/HT segment led by strong demand and robust order-book execution.

"Margins for the company are expected to be ~11.2% for the quarter with sustained robust profitability growth." The stock closed 1.71% higher at Rs.378.15 per share on BSE on Friday.

data.title: Nine dead in Erie, Pennsylvania mass shooting
data.description:
Nine people are confirmed dead in Erie, Pennsylvania, authorities said, after what Governor Josh Shapiro called a "tragic mass shooting."

The incident occurred late Friday and investigators determined that all deaths occurred before officers arrived at the scene, a statement from the city of Erie said on Saturday.

"I’ve spoken with Mayor Devlin and offered my Administration’s full support following the tragic mass shooting in Erie last night — killing nine of our fellow Pennsylvanians," Shapiro wrote in a Saturday morning post on X.

data.title: Bitcoin Tests Average Buyer’s Break-Even As ETF Outflows Clash With Wall Street Buying
data.description:
Key points:
  • Bitcoin traded almost flat on Saturday, hovering just above $82,900.
  • CryptoQuant Darkfost analyst described this level as the average holder's break-even point.
  • On Wall Street, Fidelity's FBTC bought $354.1 million of Bitcoin over 20 trading days while Morgan Stanley added 92 coins this week to reach 10,639 BTC.

Bitcoin (BTC) traded flat on Saturday, sitting just above the price at which the average holder was neither up nor down, as one analyst said the setup looked like a repeat of a pattern from late last year.

That line sat around $80,500, according to CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost. It was the cost basis of all Bitcoin in circulation, weighted by how much money went into each purchase, so when the price hovered there, the market as a whole was roughly breaking even.

Darkfost said Bitcoin was oscillating around the break-even line in a pattern that resembled late 2025 and early 2026. A market sitting on that line created doubt, he said, which pushed investors to act. For now, it was holding as support.

Analyst Ted Pillows was watching slightly higher. A weekly close above $82,700 would mean buyers are in control, he said, and could open a move toward $87,000 to $88,000.

Bitcoin’s price was trading at around $82,900, up by 0.3% at the time of writing. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around BTC remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter around it stayed at ‘low’ levels over the past day.

Who Is Still Buying

Two of the largest names on Wall Street have kept adding while the price has gone sideways. Fidelity’s FBTC fund bought $354.1 million of Bitcoin over the past 20 trading days, according to Arkham. Its other crypto funds bought in the same window, taking in $66.6 million of Ethereum (ETH) and $18.2 million of Solana (SOL). Morgan Stanley (MS) also added about 92 coins this week through its MSBT fund, Arkham data showed, lifting its total to 10,639 BTC worth roughly $880 million.

The Flows Tell A Different Story

Those two funds were buying even as the broader ETF category bled money this week. US spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $487.07 million on Wednesday, and another $244.13 million on Thursday, according to SoSoValue data. A $21.13 million inflow on Friday recovered a fraction of it.
